articles.title: Continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article first describes a simple optical experiment demonstrating diffraction and chromatic aberration using fingers against a bright background and a digital camera, connecting it to methods used in telescope mirror testing. It then transitions to an astronomical observing guide for the month, detailing the visibility of Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto, while noting Saturn and Mars are too close to the sun to be seen.

articles.title: Attend A Conjunction! AstroCon 2004 July 20-24, 2004 San Francisco Bay Area
articles.summary: AstroCon 2004, the Astronomical League's annual convention, is scheduled for July 20-24, 2004, in the San Francisco Bay Area. This event brings together major astronomical organizations, offering sessions with professional astronomers, public outreach tips, and a field trip to Lick Observatory. Attendees can find complete details and register online.

articles.title: Orbital Dynamics
articles.summary: This article delves into the orbital dynamics of the Moon, first briefly dismissing the popular 'Blue Moon' definition. It then tackles the practical question of how long the Moon remains centered in a 1-degree eyepiece field of view when using sidereal rates, detailing calculations for its angular motion and apparent size at both apogee and perigee. The author concludes that while lunar rates on telescopes can extend observation time without correction, precise alignment is crucial for their effectiveness.

articles.title: From The Board
articles.summary: The article from the SJAA board announces a request for donations of old laptops (Windows 98 or later with specific features) for club use, noting they are tax-deductible. It also discusses the possibility of creating a new SJAA logo that better represents the club's amateur star parties, suggesting a design depicting people with telescopes, and proposes a potential logo design contest for members.

articles.title: Top 10 Ways to do Astrophotography
articles.summary: This article outlines ten methods for amateur astrophotography, detailing various equipment and techniques for capturing celestial images. It covers options ranging from high-end scientific-grade CCD cameras and dedicated Schmidt cameras to more accessible approaches like modified webcams, piggyback cameras, and using a telescope as a primary lens. The guide also discusses projection eyepieces and low-cost imagers suitable for lunar and planetary photography.

articles.title: Reflections on Winning the 2004 W. Bruce Blair Medal
articles.summary: Jane Houston Jones reflects on the honor of receiving the 2004 W. Bruce Blair Medal, an award from the Western Amateur Astronomers (WAA), an organization founded by Dr. G. Bruce Blair. She delves into the history of the medal and acknowledges the inspiration she drew from past recipients, ultimately dedicating her award to John Dobson for his formative influence on her amateur astronomy journey and her commitment to sharing the universe with others.

articles.title: July General Meeting
articles.summary: The July General Meeting will feature a guest speaker, Tony Misch from Lick Observatory, discussing the latest research, the new Automatic Planet Finder (APF) telescope, and an animation of the 1882 Transit of Venus. The meeting is set for July 31 at 8:00 p.m. at Hogue Park. The document also provides comprehensive Solar System statistics for July 2004, including ephemeris data for various celestial bodies.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The article details the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner telescope program, providing information for members interested in borrowing equipment. It lists a variety of available telescopes, scopes currently on loan with their due dates, and those with extended loan periods or undergoing repair. The document also includes contact information for Mike Koop, who manages the program, and a waiting list for popular items.
